results.title: Prime two-sided ideal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A two-sided ideal $P$ of a ring $R$ is prime if $P \ne R$ and, for all $a, b \in R$, if $a r b \in P$ for every $r \in R$, then $a \in P$ or $b \in P$.

results.title: m-system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subset $M$ of a ring $R$ is an $m$-system if it is nonempty, does not contain $0$, and for all $a, b \in M$ there is some $r \in R$ with $a r b \in M$.

results.title: Jacobson's commutativity theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a ring. If for every $x \in R$ there is a natural number $n > 1$ with $x^n = x$, then $R$ is commutative, that is, $xy = yx$ for all $x, y \in R$.

results.title: Vertices of a spherically homogeneous rooted tree (Kourovka 15.14 version)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $m$ of natural numbers, the vertices of the spherically homogeneous rooted tree with branching sequence $m$ are the finite words $l_0 l_1 \cdots l_{k-1}$ of natural numbers with $l_i < m(i)$ for every $i < k$. The length of a word is its level and its prefixes are its ancestors.

results.title: Rigid vertex stabilizers (Kourovka 15.14 version)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group acting by permutations $\rho$ on the vertices of the rooted tree with branching sequence $m$, and let $v$ be a vertex. The rigid vertex stabilizer of $v$ is the set of elements $g \in G$ whose support lies in the subtree rooted at $v$: $\rho(g)$ fixes every vertex $w$ of which $v$ is not a prefix.

results.title: Rigid level stabilizers (Kourovka 15.14 version)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group acting by permutations $\rho$ on the vertices of the rooted tree with branching sequence $m$, and let $n$ be a natural number. The $n$-th rigid level stabilizer of $\rho$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by the rigid vertex stabilizers of all vertices at level $n$, the words of length $n$.

results.title: Growth rate of a finitely generated group
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Groups of exponential growth
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ has exponential growth when it is finitely generated and every finite generating family $P$ of $G$ has growth rate $\omega(G, P) > 1$.

results.title: Groups containing a free subgroup of rank two
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ contains a free subgroup of rank $2$ when there is an injective group homomorphism from the free group $F_2$ on two generators into $G$.

results.title: Full automorphism group of a binary relation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $Z$ a set and $X \subseteq Z \times Z$ a binary relation on $Z$. Then $G$ is the full automorphism group of $X$ when there is an injective group homomorphism $\varphi$ from $G$ to the group of permutations of $Z$ whose image is exactly the set of permutations $f$ of $Z$ with $(x, y) \in X \iff (f(x), f(y)) \in X$ for all $x, y \in Z$.

results.title: Birkhoff's theorem: every group is the automorphism group of a binary relation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every group $G$ there are a set $Z$ and a binary relation $X \subseteq Z \times Z$ such that $G$ is the full automorphism group of $X$: there is an injective group homomorphism $\varphi$ from $G$ to the group of permutations of $Z$ whose image is exactly the set of permutations $f$ of $Z$ with $(x, y) \in X \iff (f(x), f(y)) \in X$ for all $x, y \in Z$.

results.title: One-element sets are difference smooth

results.title: Maynard–Tao theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $m \ge 2$ there is a natural number $k$ such that for every admissible finite set $H$ of at least $k$ integers there are infinitely many integers $n$ for which $n + h$ is a (positive) prime for at least $m$ elements $h \in H$.

results.title: Prime $m$-tuples with smooth gaps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 2$ and $k$ be natural numbers such that every admissible finite set $H$ of at least $k$ integers has infinitely many integers $n$ for which $n + h$ is a (positive) prime for at least $m$ elements $h \in H$. Then there are infinitely many $m$-tuples of primes $p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_m$ such that for all $j < i$ every prime factor of $p_i - p_j$ is at most $k$.

results.title: Prime pairs with $5$-smooth difference under Elliott–Halberstam

results.title: Admissible difference-smooth sets of every size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$ there is an admissible set $H$ of exactly $k$ integers that is difference $k$-smooth: for all distinct $h, h' \in H$, every prime factor of $h - h'$ is at most $k$.

results.title: Admissible sets are not difference smooth at small bounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be an admissible finite set of $k \ge 2$ integers, let $z \le k$ be a prime and let $\ell < z$ be a natural number. Then $H$ is not difference $\ell$-smooth. Equivalently, $H$ is not difference $\ell$-smooth for any $\ell$ less than the largest prime at most $k$.

results.title: Root of a binomial tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The root of the binomial tree with rank $r$, root value $a$ and list of children $c$ is $a$.

results.title: Children of a binomial tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The children of a binomial tree are the binomial trees in the list stored at its root node, in their stored order.

results.title: Elements of a binomial tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The multiset of elements of a binomial tree with root value $x$ and children $t_1, \dots, t_k$ is defined recursively as $\{x\}$ added to the multiset sum of the multisets of elements of $t_1, \dots, t_k$; the stored rank plays no role.

results.title: The root of a binomial tree is one of its elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every binomial tree $t$, the root of $t$ occurs in the multiset represented by $t$.

results.title: Valid binomial tree
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$, validity of binomial trees over $\alpha$ is defined inductively: the tree with stored rank $r$, root $a$ and list of children $c_1, \dots, c_k$ is valid when every child $c_i$ is valid, the ranks of $c_1, \dots, c_k$ are exactly $r - 1, r - 2, \dots, 0$ in this order, the multiset of elements of the tree (its root together with the elements of all its children) has exactly…

results.title: Singleton binomial heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a value $a$ in a linear order, the binomial heap whose list of trees consists of exactly one tree: the tree of rank $0$ with root $a$ and no children.

results.title: Linking two binomial trees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Over a linear order, the link of binomial trees $s$ and $t$ is defined as follows. If the root of $s$ is at most the root of $t$, it is the tree whose rank is one more than the rank of $s$, whose root is the root of $s$, and whose children are $t$ followed by the children of $s$. Otherwise it is the tree whose rank is one more than the rank of $s$, whose root is the root of $t$, and whose children are $s$ followed…

results.title: Linking binomial trees adds their elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For any two binomial trees $s$ and $t$ over a linearly ordered type, the multiset of elements of the tree obtained by linking $s$ and $t$ is the sum of the multisets of elements of $s$ and $t$.

results.title: Singleton binomial trees are valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and any $a \in \alpha$, the singleton binomial tree with rank $0$, root $a$ and no children is valid.

results.title: Children of a valid binomial tree are valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$, every child of a valid binomial tree over $\alpha$ is itself a valid binomial tree.

results.title: Child ranks of a valid binomial tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$, if a valid binomial tree over $\alpha$ has rank $r$, then the ranks of its children, listed in their stored order, are $r - 1, r - 2, \dots, 1, 0$; there are no children when $r = 0$.

results.title: Size of a valid binomial tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$, every valid binomial tree of rank $r$ over $\alpha$ represents a multiset of exactly $2^r$ elements, counted with multiplicity.

results.title: The rank of a valid binomial tree is logarithmic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A valid binomial tree of rank $r$ holding $n$ elements, counted with multiplicity, satisfies $r \le \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$.

results.title: The root of a valid binomial tree is a lower bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$ and a valid binomial tree $t$ over $\alpha$, the root $a$ of $t$ satisfies $a \le v$ for every element $v$ of the multiset represented by $t$.

results.title: Linking preserves binomial-tree validity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $s$ and $t$ are valid binomial trees of equal rank, then the tree obtained by linking $s$ with $t$ is valid.

results.title: Valid binomial forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$, a list of binomial trees over $\alpha$ is a valid forest when every tree in it is a valid binomial tree and the ranks of its trees are strictly increasing along the list.

results.title: Elements of a binomial forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The multiset of elements of a list of binomial trees $t_1, \dots, t_k$ is the multiset sum of the multisets of elements of $t_1, \dots, t_k$; for the empty list it is the empty multiset.

results.title: Rank lower bound for a forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $r$, a list of binomial trees has ranks at least $r$ when every tree in it has rank at least $r$.

results.title: The empty forest is valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$, the empty list of binomial trees over $\alpha$ is a valid binomial forest.

results.title: Validity of binomial forests passes to sublists
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$ and lists $L$, $R$ of binomial trees over $\alpha$, if $L$ is a sublist of $R$ (obtained by deleting entries while keeping the order of the rest) and $R$ is a valid forest, then $L$ is a valid forest.

results.title: Tree ranks in a valid forest are logarithmic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $F$ is a valid binomial forest and $T$ is a tree of $F$ of rank $r$, then $r \le \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$, where $n$ is the number of elements, counted with multiplicity, represented by $F$.

results.title: A valid binomial forest has logarithmically many trees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a relation $\le$. If a valid binomial forest over $\alpha$ has $n$ elements, counted with multiplicity, then it consists of at most $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$ trees, where $\lfloor \log_2 0 \rfloor$ is taken to be $0$.

results.title: A valid binomial forest with no elements has no trees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a relation $\le$. If a list of binomial trees over $\alpha$ is a valid binomial forest and its multiset of elements has cardinality $0$, then the list has length $0$.

results.title: Carry insertion into a binomial forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a linearly ordered type, the carry of a binomial tree $t$ into a list $F$ of binomial trees is defined by recursion on $F$. If $F$ is empty, the result is the one-tree list $[t]$. If $F$ starts with a tree $u$ followed by a list $F'$ and the rank of $t$ is less than the rank of $u$, the result is $F$ with $t$ prepended. Otherwise the result is the carry of the link of $t$ and $u$ into $F'$.

results.title: Melding binomial forests
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Over a linear order, the meld of two lists of binomial trees is defined by recursion on their total length. For every list $L$, the meld of the empty list with $L$ is $L$, and the meld of $L$ with the empty list is $L$. For nonempty lists with first trees $s$ and $t$ and remaining lists $F$ and $G$: if the rank of $s$ is less than the rank of $t$, the meld is $s$ followed by the meld of $F$ with the second list; if…

results.title: Melding binomial forests adds their elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For any two lists $L$ and $R$ of binomial trees over a linearly ordered type, the multiset of elements of the meld of $L$ and $R$ is the sum of the multisets of elements of $L$ and $R$.

results.title: Melding preserves forest validity and rank lower bounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number and let $F$ and $G$ be valid binomial forests in which every tree has rank at least $r$. Then the meld of $F$ and $G$ is a valid binomial forest in which every tree has rank at least $r$.

results.title: Removing a minimum-root tree from a forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $T$ of binomial trees over a linear order, the result is nothing when $T$ is empty. Otherwise it is the first tree $m$ of $T$ whose root is minimal among the roots of the trees of $T$, together with the list obtained from $T$ by deleting that occurrence of $m$, the remaining trees keeping their order.

results.title: Removing a minimum-root tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a list of binomial trees over a linear order, and suppose that removing a minimum tree from $T$ returns the tree $m$ and the list $R$. Then the multiset represented by $m$ plus the multiset represented by the forest $R$ equals the multiset represented by the forest $T$; $m$ is a member of $T$; $R$ is a sublist of $T$; and the root of $m$ is at most the root of every tree in $T$.

results.title: Reversed children of a valid binomial tree form a valid forest
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and a valid binomial tree $t$ over $\alpha$, the children of $t$ listed in reverse order form a valid binomial forest: every tree in the list is valid and the ranks strictly increase along the list.

results.title: Binomial heap
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A binomial min-heap over a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ consists of a list of binomial trees over $\alpha$ together with a proof that this list is a valid binomial forest: every tree in it is a valid binomial tree and the tree ranks are strictly increasing along the list.

results.title: Elements of a binomial heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Over a linearly ordered type, the multiset of elements of a binomial heap is the multiset of elements of its list of binomial trees, that is, the multiset sum of the multisets of elements of its trees.

results.title: Tree ranks in a binomial heap are logarithmic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every tree in a binomial heap holding $n$ elements, counted with multiplicity, has rank at most $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$.

results.title: A binomial heap has logarithmically many trees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a binomial heap over a linearly ordered type has $n$ elements, counted with multiplicity, then its number of trees is at most $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$, where $\lfloor \log_2 0 \rfloor$ is taken to be $0$.

results.title: Empty binomial heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, the empty binomial heap over $\alpha$ is the binomial heap whose list of trees is empty.

results.title: Melding binomial heaps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Over a linear order, the meld of two binomial heaps is the binomial heap whose forest is the meld of the forests of the two heaps.

results.title: One-element binomial heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a value $a$ in a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, the one-element binomial heap of $a$ is the binomial heap whose list of trees consists of exactly one tree: the binomial tree of rank $0$ with root $a$ and no children.

results.title: Insertion into a binomial heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Inserting a value $x$ into a binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type gives the meld of the one-element binomial heap containing $x$ with $H$.

results.title: Minimum of a binomial heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The minimum lookup of a binomial heap over a linearly ordered type returns no value when the heap has no trees, and otherwise returns the least of the root values of its trees, leaving the heap unchanged.

results.title: Minimum deletion on a binomial forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a list of binomial trees over a linearly ordered type, if the list is empty there is no result. Otherwise, remove the first tree whose root is minimal among the roots of the list; the result is the root of that tree together with the forest obtained by melding its children, in reversed order, with the remaining trees.

results.title: Deleting the minimum of a binomial heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: If the binomial heap $H$ has no trees, there is no result. Otherwise, remove from the list of trees of $H$ the first tree whose root is minimal; the result is that root together with the binomial heap whose list of trees is obtained by melding the children of the removed tree, in reversed order, with the remaining trees.

results.title: Binomial heap deletion agrees with forest deletion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, deleting the minimum of $H$ and then replacing the remaining heap by its list of trees gives the same result as minimum deletion on the list of trees of $H$: both have no result, or both return the same minimum value and the same list of trees.

results.title: Melding binomial heaps adds their elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For any two binomial heaps $H_1$ and $H_2$ over a linearly ordered type, the multiset of elements of the meld of $H_1$ and $H_2$ is the sum of the multisets of elements of $H_1$ and $H_2$.

results.title: Insertion into a binomial heap adds one occurrence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type and every value $v$, the multiset of elements of the heap obtained by inserting $v$ into $H$ is the multiset of elements of $H$ with one more occurrence of $v$.

results.title: The minimum lookup fails exactly on the empty binomial heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, the minimum lookup of $H$ returns no value if and only if the list of trees of $H$ is empty.

results.title: The minimum lookup of a binomial heap returns one of its elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a binomial heap over a linearly ordered type. If the minimum lookup of $H$ returns $m$, then $m$ is an element of $H$.

results.title: The minimum lookup of a binomial heap returns a lower bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a binomial heap over a linearly ordered type. If the minimum lookup of $H$ returns $m$, then $m \le v$ for every element $v$ of $H$.

results.title: Deleting the minimum fails only on the empty binomial heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, deleting the minimum of $H$ returns no result if and only if the list of trees of $H$ is empty.

results.title: Deleting the minimum of a binomial heap removes one occurrence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, if deleting the minimum of $H$ succeeds and returns a value $m$ and a heap $H'$, then the multiset of elements of $H'$ is the multiset of elements of $H$ with one occurrence of $m$ removed.

results.title: Deleting the minimum of a binomial heap splits its multiset
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, if deleting the minimum of $H$ succeeds and returns a value $m$ and a heap $H'$, then the multiset of elements of $H$ equals the multiset of elements of $H'$ with one more occurrence of $m$.

results.title: The value deleted from a binomial heap is a lower bound for its elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If deleting the minimum of a binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type succeeds and returns a value $m$ together with a remaining heap, then $m \le v$ for every value $v$ in the multiset of elements of $H$.
